title: Synthesis of USP-Grade 89Zr-Panitumumab for Medical Use
protocol: Transfer 0.5 mL (10 mg) of panitumumab from the vial to a microcentrifuge tube.
Adjust the pH of the solution to 9.0 by administering 0.1 M Na2CO3 with a metal-free pipette tip and pH paper.
Add 0.4 mL of 0.9% saline to make an overall volume of 1.0 mL.
Transfer 10 μL of 20 mM DFO stock solution in DMSO over the panitumumab using a metal-free sterile micropipette tip.
Incubate the reaction for 30 to 60 min at 37 °C using a Thermomixer.
Equilibrate a PD10 column with 20 mL of 0.9% NaCl solution (USP).
Pipette the reaction mixture onto the PD10 column and discard the flow-through.
Pipette 1.5 ml of 0.9% NaCl onto the column and discard the flow-through.
Pipette 2 mL of 0.9% NaCl onto the PD-10 column and collect the DFO-protein in 0.5 mL fractions.
Combine fractions 2 to 4 to get DFO-conjugated protein in a 4 mL glass vial.
Transfer 20 µL of the product to a microcentrifuge tube containing 0.5 mL of saline (diluted to 500 times).
Inject 20 µL of this diluted sample to the HPLC instrument.
Integrate the HPLC chromatogram to get the UV peak area at 280 nm.
Calculate the protein concentration using the standard calibration curve.
Calculate the volume needed for 1 mg protein.
Pipette the required volume (4-5 mCi, ~250 μL) of 89Zr oxalic acid solution into a reaction vial.
Calibrate the reaction vial using a dose calibrator to determine the amount of activity in mCi.
Pipette an adequate amount of 2M Na2CO3 (~100 μL) into the reaction vial.
Incubate for 3 min at room temperature.
Adjust pH of reaction solution to 7.5 using 2M Na2CO3.
Gently shake and add 0.5 ml 0.5M HEPES (pH7.2).
Add adequate volume of conjugate to get 1-1.2 mg mass of the conjugate.
Add 0.2 mL gentisic acid solution.
Incubate the reaction for 1 h at room temperature with occasional gentle shaking.
Dilute approximately 2 μL of crude product to 500 times with 0.9% NaCl.
Perform the ITLC experiment by pipetting ~1 µL of diluted sample to the ITLC plate.
Develop the ITLC plate in the developing chamber using 20 mM of citric acid solution as the mobile phase.
Cut the plate in middle and count both the bottom and top parts separately for radioactivity in a gamma well counter.
Calculate RCY using this equation: RCY(%) = (counts of the bottom / counts of (top + bottom)) X 100.
If RCY is < 50%, discard the whole batch and start new labeling reaction.
Rinse/equilibrate a PD-10 column with 20 mL of the mobile phase.
Pipette the conjugation reaction mixture onto the column and discard the flow-through.
Pipette 1.5 mL of the mobile phase onto the column and discard the flow-through.
Pipette 2 mL of the mobile phase onto the PD-10 column.
Collect the 89Zr-DFO-protein at 0.5 mL fractions in small glass vials.
Collect the 89Zr-DFO-protein at 1.5 mL fractions in small glass vials.
Check amount of activity of each fraction in dose calibrator.
Pipette 0.5 mL of the mobile phase onto the PD-10 column.
Collect it as a 3rd fraction.
Check amount of activity in dose calibrator.
Check radiochemical purity of fraction two with ITLC.
Check radiochemical purity of fraction three with ITLC.
Combine fractions two and three in a 10 mL vial if they are > 90% pure.
Check the amount of radioactivity using a dose calibrator.
Dilute the product to 5 mL using 0.9% saline.
Draw the product solution in a 10 mL syringe.
Remove the needle and attach a sterile filter.
Connect the filter needle to a 10 mL sterile vial with a venting needle.
Pass the solution through the sterile syringe filter slowly by pressing the plunger of the syringe.
Perform bubble point test of the sterile filter following the standard procedure.
Detach the product vial from the syringe attached to the sterile filter.
Assay the product vial for total radioactivity in a dose calibrator.
Visually inspect the vial for particulates and color.
Place the sterilizing filter on a gas line with a pressure gauge and the outlet under water.
Increase the gas pressure slowly until a steady stream of bubbles is observed at the filter outlet.
Record the pressure at which the bubble stream begins.
Compare the recorded pressure with the manufacturer’s rating (≥ 46 psi) for the filter.
Withdraw 300 µL of the product after a successful filter integrity test for further QC and sterility testing.
Complete a blank injection before sample injection to ensure there are no impurities from the column or instrument.
Inject 20 µL of 89Zr-panitumumab (preferably via auto-injection).
Integrate all UV and radiation responses to obtain peak areas for [89Zr]-panitumumab.
Perform reverse correlation from the linear equation of DFO-panitumab to determine the concentration of \[89Zr]-panitumumab in the final solution.
Integrate any other 280 nm UV absorbing chromatographic peaks that elute after 3.0 minutes and before 40 minutes post injection individually.
Calculate the sum of these peaks as a percentage, which should be less than “10%” in the final product.
Integrate all radioactive peaks in the chromatogram.
Calculate the percent of \[89Zr]-panitumumab radioactivity in the final product, which should exceed 90%.
Transfer 0.5 mL of ITLC eluent to a 15 mL centrifuge tube for developing chamber preparation.
Using a micro pipette, spot ~1 µL of sample at the origin of the ITLC strip.
Allow the spotted area on the ITLC strip to dry before placing it in the developing chamber.
Develop the ITLC plate by carefully positioning it in the developing chamber.
Wait until the solvent front has migrated at least 90% of the length of the ITLC plate.
Cut the ITLC plate into two parts and place each part in separate counting tubes.
Count for radioactivity with an appropriate counter.
Calculate the radiochemical purity using this equation: RCP(%) = (counts of the bottom / counts of (top + bottom)) × 100.
Check pH test strips by pipetting pH 5 and pH 7 calibrated commercial pH standards onto individual strips.
Ensure the color on the pH test strips matches the pH 5 and pH 7 on the color key supplied with the test strips.
Pipette 89Zr-panitumumab onto another pH test strip, then check the color against the color key.
Verify that the measured pH is between pH 6 to 8.
Test levels of bacterial endotoxin in 89Zr-panitumumab using PTS Limulus Amebocyte Lysate (LAL) Test with Endosafe®-PTS portable test system from Charles River Laboratories.
